sources.title: Solomon Islands eVisa: Tourist allowed-nationalities dataset
sources.officialityEvidence: The live Immigration Division visitor page links this Government eVisa host. The public Tourist-product endpoint returned a closed JSON nationality list during the current replay; neither Macao nor Montenegro appears.

sources.title: Visitor Visa – Tourist
sources.officialityEvidence: The current Immigration Division page links the Government online application, describes online submission and says an approved visa grant letter is emailed for presentation at entry.
sources.supportingExcerpt: Once your visa is approved, we will send your visa grant letter through your email.

sources.title: Visas
sources.officialityEvidence: The live Immigration Division category page says online application and payment are operational for visitor visa classes, but it does not assign every passport nationality to that service.
sources.supportingExcerpt: Online Application and Payment is now Operational

sources.title: Solomon Islands: visa regime for citizens of Montenegro
sources.publisher: Government of Montenegro, Ministry of Foreign Affairs
sources.officialityEvidence: The current Montenegro Government country page directly requires its citizens to possess a visa for Solomon Islands and notes that no resident mission exists, but does not identify the issuance route.
sources.supportingExcerpt: Citizens of Montenegro must possess a visa to enter Solomon Islands.

unresolved.reason: Solomon Islands' current Tourist eVisa nationality dataset does not identify the Macao SAR passport, and the generic online visitor guidance does not establish an unlisted-nationality complement. No PRC nationality or document result is transferred to Macao.

Montenegro's current Government page establishes visa liability but not whether issuance is electronic or consular. Solomon Islands' generic online visitor guidance does not override the Tourist eVisa dataset's lack of a Montenegro result, and omission is not treated as a residual route.
